mainTopic: דוד's נסיון with בת שבע: his failure, his prayers in תהלים, and his forgiveness through יסורין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a פסוק about אחיתופל. Then רב יהודה in the name of רב teaches that a person should never bring himself into a נסיון, because דוד asked God to test him and failed. The גמרא tells how the test with בת שבע happened: דוד's plan to calm his desire backfired, and the שטן, disguised as a bird, caused him to see her. רבא then brings a series of פסוקים from תהלים as דוד's own words about the sin: his regret, his plea for forgiveness, the idea that בת שבע was meant for him from creation but taken too early, and his reply to mockers that public shaming is worse than his sin. רב יהודה adds that דוד once wanted to serve עבודה זרה while fleeing אבשלום, and חושי talked him out of it using the סמוכין of יפת תואר and בן סורר ומורה. רבי דוסתאי describes דוד bargaining for forgiveness step by step. He is forgiven, but his sin must stay written in the תנ"ך, and full atonement comes only through יסורין. The amud ends with רב's teaching that דוד suffered six months of צרעת, lost the שכינה, and was avoided by the סנהדרין. The proof of the six months continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the verse about the one who ate my bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a פסוק from תהלים that was being used about אחיתופל, who learned Torah with דוד and then turned against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: "...who ate my bread has lifted his heel against me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a פסוק it started quoting just before this, about אחיתופל turning against דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Bread' here stands for Torah that אחיתופל shared with דוד. The point of the פסוק is that someone close to דוד, who learned with him, betrayed him. This wraps up the earlier discussion before the גמרא moves to a new teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: My bread (here a picture for Torah learning)
Heel; 'lifting a heel' means turning against someone
דוד's advisor who later betrayed him

phrases.english: who ate my bread has lifted his heel against me.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a פסוק (תהלים 41:10) whose beginning was quoted just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a verse quoted in the preceding discussion about אחיתופל.
steps.raayaObject: That אחיתופל, who shared Torah with דוד, turned against him.

steps.title: Never bring yourself into a test
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב teaches that a person should never put himself into a נסיון, since דוד did and failed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should never bring himself into a test, because דוד, king of Israel, brought himself into a test and failed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: רב warns that a person should never ask for or walk into a test of his character.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is backed by a real example: even דוד המלך, a great צדיק, asked to be tested and failed. If someone that great failed, an ordinary person surely should not invite a test. The next steps tell the story behind this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A test or trial of a person's character

steps.whatToRemember: The main lesson of the whole story: never invite a נסיון on yourself.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A person should never bring himself
into a test,
for David, king of Israel,
brought himself into a test and failed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לְעוֹלָם אַל יָבִיא אָדָם עַצְמוֹ לִידֵי נִסָּיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new aggadic teaching connected to the theme of דוד's troubles.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should never put himself into a נסיון, as shown by דוד, who did so and failed.

steps.title: דוד asks why God is not called the God of דוד
steps.stepSummary: דוד asks הקב"ה why people mention the אבות in prayer but do not say 'God of דוד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said before God: Master of the World, why do people say 'God of אברהם, God of יצחק, and God of יעקב,' but they do not say 'God of דוד'?
steps.whatsHappening: The story begins: דוד asks God why his name is not joined to God's name the way the אבות' names are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד wants the same honor as the אבות, having God's name linked with his own. This question sets up God's answer, which explains what made the אבות different.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the World (a way of speaking to God)

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
phrases.notes: 'He' is דוד, speaking to God.

phrases.english: why do people say
"God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob,"
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of the first ברכה of the עמידה.

phrases.english: and they do not say "God of David"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, מִפְּנֵי מָה אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that proves רב's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the אבות have God's name linked to them in prayer, but דוד does not.

steps.title: God answers: they were tested and you were not
steps.stepSummary: הקב"ה explains that the אבות earned this honor by passing tests, and דוד had not been tested.
steps.simpleTranslation: God said: They were tested by Me, and you have not been tested by Me.
steps.whatsHappening: God answers דוד's question: the אבות went through tests, and that is why His name is linked to theirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honor of 'God of אברהם' came from passing real tests of faith. דוד had not faced such a test. This answer is what leads דוד to ask to be tested.

phrases.english: He said: They were tested by Me,
phrases.notes: 'He' is God now, answering דוד.

phrases.english: and you have not been tested by Me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: אִינְהוּ מִינְּסוּ לִי וְאַתְּ לָא מִינַּסֵּית לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers דוד's question from the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אבות passed tests before God; דוד had not been tested.

steps.title: דוד asks to be tested
steps.stepSummary: דוד asks God to test him, quoting his own פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said before Him: Master of the World, examine me and test me, as it says: "Examine me, ה׳, and test me..."
steps.whatsHappening: דוד responds by asking God to test him, which is exactly what רב warned against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the moment where דוד 'brings himself into a נסיון.' The גמרא connects his request to a real פסוק that דוד wrote in תהלים. This request is the mistake that רב's rule is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think דוד was punished just for wanting to be close to God. The problem the גמרא points to is that he asked for a test, instead of asking to be kept away from one.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
examine me and test me, as it is stated:
"Examine me, Lord, and test me, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 26:2

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, בְּחָנֵנִי וְנַסֵּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: דוד reacts to God's answer by requesting a test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד asks to be tested, supported by his פסוק in תהלים.

steps.title: God agrees and even tells דוד what the test will be
steps.stepSummary: God agrees to test דוד and gives him an advantage the אבות did not have: He tells him ahead of time that the test will involve ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: God said: I will test you, and I will do something special for you. I did not tell them what their test was, but I am telling you that I will test you with a matter of forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: God accepts דוד's request and reveals the kind of test in advance, something He never did for the אבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This makes the test seem easier: דוד knows exactly what is coming and can prepare. That makes his failure even more striking, and it sets up רב יהודה's explanation of how his preparation backfired.

phrases.english: He said: I will test you,
and I will do something special with you,
for them I did not inform,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the אבות; they were not told ahead of time what their test would be.

phrases.english: whereas I am informing you
that I will test you with a matter of forbidden relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: מְינַסֵּינָא לָךְ, וְעָבֵידְנָא מִילְּתָא בַּהֲדָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: God responds to דוד's request for a test.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God agrees and tells דוד ahead of time that the test will involve ערוה.

steps.title: Right away, דוד rises from his bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the test began immediately, quoting the פסוק that opens the story of בת שבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately: "And it was at evening time, and דוד rose from his bed..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the test started right away, using the פסוק that begins the story of דוד and בת שבע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'immediately' ties the פסוק directly to God's warning. The detail that דוד got up from his bed in the evening will be explained by רב יהודה in the next step.

phrases.english: Immediately: "And it came to pass at evening time
that David rose from his bed, etc."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 11:2. This is where דוד sees בת שבע from the roof.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד, ״וַיְהִי לְעֵת הָעֶרֶב וַיָּקׇם דָּוִד מֵעַל מִשְׁכָּבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the test announced in the previous step beginning at once.
steps.raayaObject: That the promised test of ערוה came right away.

steps.title: דוד's plan backfired: feeding desire makes it hungrier
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that דוד moved his marital relations to the daytime to calm his desire, but he forgot that satisfying this desire only makes it stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: He turned his nighttime bed into his daytime bed, and a teaching slipped from his mind: There is a small limb in a person; if he satisfies it, it is hungry, and if he starves it, it is satisfied.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains why דוד was getting up from his bed in the evening, and why his plan to protect himself failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the test would involve ערוה, דוד tried to tire out his desire by being with his wives during the day. But he forgot a basic rule: indulging this desire makes it grow, while holding back calms it. So his preparation actually made him weaker when the test came.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching was hidden from him (he forgot it)

steps.whatToRemember: Feeding a desire does not quiet it; it makes it hungrier. Holding back is what brings calm. This is why דוד's preparation failed, and why one should not invite a נסיון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It completes the proof of רב's rule: even with advance warning and a plan, דוד failed. A person cannot count on outsmarting his יצר.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
That he turned his nighttime bed
into his daytime bed,
phrases.notes: He means דוד was with his wives during the day, hoping to calm his desire before the test.

phrases.english: and a teaching slipped from his mind:
There is a small limb in a person;
if he satisfies it, it is hungry,
and if he starves it, it is satisfied.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שֶׁהָפַךְ מִשְׁכָּבוֹ שֶׁל לַיְלָה לְמִשְׁכָּבוֹ שֶׁל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in the previous step and why דוד's preparation failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד tried to weaken his desire by indulging it, forgetting that indulgence only increases it.

steps.title: The שטן appears as a bird and דוד sees בת שבע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about דוד seeing a woman bathing and explains how it happened: the שטן, disguised as a bird, caused the screen hiding בת שבע to break.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he walked on the roof of the king's house, and from the roof he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was very beautiful.' בת שבע was washing her hair behind a beehive. The שטן came and looked to דוד like a bird. דוד shot an arrow at it. The arrow split the beehive, she was uncovered, and he saw her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story behind the פסוק, showing exactly how דוד came to see בת שבע. This is the test God had warned him about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says דוד saw a woman bathing. The גמרא adds that she was actually hidden, and the שטן set up a trap so that she would be seen. This is the test דוד had asked for, now coming to him in a way he did not expect.

keyTerms.meaning: A beehive (or woven basket) that was screening her
The שטן, the force that tests people

phrases.english: "And he walked upon the roof of the king's house,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 11:2

phrases.english: and he saw a woman bathing from the roof,
and the woman was very beautiful to look at."

phrases.aramaic: בַּת שֶׁבַע הֲוָה קָא חָיְיפָא רֵישָׁא
phrases.english: בת שבע was washing her hair
behind a beehive.
The שטן came and appeared to him as a bird.
He shot an arrow at it; it split the beehive,
she was exposed, and he saw her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after רב יהודה's comment about דוד's state of mind, now showing the moment the test came.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's seeing בת שבע was set up by the שטן disguised as a bird.

steps.title: דוד falls immediately
steps.stepSummary: Right after seeing her, דוד sends for בת שבע and lives with her, as the פסוקים describe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately the פסוק says: 'And דוד sent and asked about the woman, and someone said: Isn't this בת שבע, daughter of אליעם, wife of אוריה the Hittite? And דוד sent messengers and took her, and she came to him and he lay with her, and she had purified herself from her impurity, and she went back to her house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that דוד failed the test right away, quoting the next פסוקים in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'immediately' is the key point: there was no gap between seeing her and acting. Even though God had warned him in advance, דוד did not hold back.

phrases.english: Immediately: "And דוד sent and inquired after the woman,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 11:3-4

phrases.english: and one said: Is this not בת שבע,
daughter of אליעם, wife of אוריה the Hittite?
And דוד sent messengers and took her,
and she came to him and he lay with her,
and she had purified herself from her impurity,
and she returned to her house."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: right after seeing her, דוד acts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד failed the test right away.

steps.title: A פסוק in תהלים describes this test
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that a פסוק in תהלים, about God testing דוד's heart at night, refers to this very episode.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'You tested my heart, You visited me at night, You refined me but did not find; my wicked thought should not pass my mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story to a פסוק in תהלים, reading it as דוד describing his own test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'You tested my heart' and 'You visited me at night' fit the test that God sent him. The end of the פסוק, about what came out of his mouth, is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written
You refined me (like metal in a fire)

phrases.english: And that is what is written:
"You have tested my heart, You have visited me at night,
phrases.notes: תהלים 17:3

phrases.english: You have refined me, but You will not find;
my thought should not have passed my mouth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After telling the story, the גמרא shows a פסוק that reflects it.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד was tested and failed in this episode.

steps.title: דוד regrets asking to be tested
steps.stepSummary: דוד wishes his mouth had been shut so that he never asked God to test him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: If only a muzzle had fallen on the mouth of my enemy, so I would never have said such a thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the end of the פסוק: דוד regrets the words he said when he asked God to test him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads 'זמותי' as 'זממא', a muzzle. דוד is saying he wishes he had been muzzled before he asked for the test back in step 5. His failure came from that request.
steps.whatToRemember: דוד asked to be tested, failed, and looked back on that request with regret.

phrases.english: He said: If only a muzzle had fallen
phrases.notes: A play on זַמֹּתִי in the פסוק, read here as זְמָמָא, a muzzle.

phrases.english: on the mouth of the one who hates me,
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying 'on my own mouth.'

phrases.english: and I would not have said such a thing!
phrases.notes: He means his request back in step 5: 'Test me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last words of the פסוק quoted in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד regretted asking to be tested.

steps.title: Don't let them say a bird brought down the mountain
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads a פסוק in תהלים as דוד asking forgiveness, so people won't mock that a great man was brought down by a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'For the conductor, by דוד: In ה׳ I trusted; how can you say to my soul, Flee to your mountain, bird'? דוד said to הקב"ה: Master of the world, forgive me for that sin, so that people will not say, 'The mountain among you was chased away by a bird.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching from רבא. He reads another פסוק in תהלים as דוד's plea for forgiveness after the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא splits the word 'הרכם' into 'הר שבכם', 'the mountain among you,' meaning דוד, the great leader. Since the whole thing started with a bird (the שטן in disguise), דוד feared people would say a bird brought down the great man. He asks forgiveness so his downfall won't become a joke.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: רבא taught: What is the meaning of what is written:
"For the conductor, by דוד: In Hashem I trusted;
phrases.notes: תהלים 11:1

phrases.aramaic: אֵיךְ תֹּאמְרוּ לְנַפְשִׁי נוּדִי הַרְכֶם צִפֹּר״?
phrases.english: how can you say to my soul: Flee to your mountain, bird"?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: דוד said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, מְחוֹל לִי עַל אוֹתוֹ עָוֹן
phrases.english: Master of the world, forgive me for that sin,
so that they will not say: "The mountain among you, a bird chased him away."
phrases.notes: 'Mountain' is דוד, the great one; the 'bird' is the bird from step 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story itself to דוד's later prayer about it, linking to the bird from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד asked forgiveness so that people would not say a bird brought down a great man.

steps.title: דוד could have controlled himself, but God's words had to come true
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads another פסוק as דוד saying he could have beaten his desire, but did not, so that people would not say the servant proved his Master wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'Against You alone I sinned, and I did what is evil in Your eyes, so that You are right in Your words and pure in Your judgment'? דוד said to הקב"ה: It is clear and known before You that if I had wanted to hold back my desire, I could have. But I said: let them not say, 'The servant beat his master.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching from רבא. He explains a פסוק in תהלים as דוד telling God why he did not overcome the test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God had announced the test and even told דוד exactly what it would be (step 6). The פסוק says 'so that You are right in Your words.' רבא reads this to mean דוד chose not to hold back, so that nobody could say the servant had beaten the Master who tested him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is revealed and known before You
To hold back my evil inclination
So that You will be proven right

steps.whatToRemember: דוד's story moves from asking for a test, to failing it, to regretting it, to asking forgiveness, to explaining that his failure proved God's words true.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the sin was fine or that דוד had no choice. He clearly says he could have held back, and in the earlier steps he regrets it and asks forgiveness.

phrases.english: רבא taught: What is the meaning of what is written:
"Against You, You alone, I have sinned,
phrases.notes: תהלים 51:6

phrases.english: and I have done what is evil in Your eyes,
so that You will be right in Your words and pure in Your judgment"?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: דוד said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
It is revealed and known before You

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי בְּעַאי לְמִכְפְּיֵיהּ לְיִצְרַי הֲוָה כָּיֵיפְינָא,
phrases.english: that if I had wanted to hold back my desire, I would have held it back,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמֵינָא דְּלָא לֵימְרוּ ״עַבְדָּא זַכְיֵהּ לְמָרֵיהּ״.
phrases.english: but I said: so that they will not say, "The servant beat his master."
phrases.notes: He means: if I had passed, people would say the servant got the better of his Master, who was the one testing him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבא on a פסוק in תהלים about the same sin, now explaining why דוד did not hold back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד could have controlled himself, but did not, so that God's statement would be proven true.

steps.title: בת שבע was meant for דוד from Creation
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads 'כי אני לצלע נכון' as saying בת שבע was meant for דוד from creation, but she came to him through pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'For I am ready for צלע, and my pain is always before me'? בת שבע daughter of אליעם was meant for דוד from the six days of creation. But she came to him through pain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains a פסוק in תהלים as דוד saying that בת שבע was always meant to be his. The problem was only the painful way he got her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word צלע also means 'side' or 'rib', like the rib that חוה was made from. So רבא reads it as 'I was set up with my matching partner.' The second half, 'my pain is always before me', tells us that the way it happened brought him lasting pain.

keyTerms.meaning: Rib or side; here a hint to a destined wife, like חוה

phrases.english: Rava taught:
What is the meaning of that which is written
"For I am ready to stumble [letzela]
phrases.notes: תהלים 38:18. צלע can also mean 'rib', like the rib חוה was made from; that's the hint רבא uses.

phrases.english: and my pain is always before me"?

phrases.aramaic: רְאוּיָה הָיְתָה בַּת שֶׁבַע בַּת אֱלִיעָם
phrases.english: Bathsheba, daughter of Eliam, was fit
for David from the six days of Creation,
but she came to him through pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another of רבא's readings of תהלים as דוד speaking about the בת שבע episode
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בת שבע was destined for דוד from creation, but he got her through pain.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל says the same: he took the fruit unripe
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from דבי רבי ישמעאל backs up רבא: בת שבע was meant for דוד, but he 'ate her unripe'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: בת שבע daughter of אליעם was meant for דוד, but he ate her while she was still unripe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an older teaching that says the same thing as רבא. This supports his idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture is a fruit that would have been his anyway, but he picked it before it was ripe. The teaching adds that his mistake was about timing. She was not someone forbidden to him forever.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise; brings a matching source
A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: בת שבע was meant for דוד. His sin was taking her too early and in the wrong way.

phrases.english: And likewise, the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Fit for David was
Bathsheba, daughter of Eliam,
but he partook of her unripe.
phrases.notes: Picture a fruit eaten before it is ready. He took her before the proper time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's teaching in step 15 with a matching ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that בת שבע was destined for דוד
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל: 'אכלה פגה'

steps.title: דוד's enemies tore at him, but he had no blood left
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads 'קרעו ולא דמו' as דוד telling God that even if they tore his flesh, no blood would flow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'When I limped they rejoiced and gathered, the wretched gathered against me, and those I do not know; they tore and did not stop'? דוד said to God: Master of the world, You know that if they tore my flesh, my blood would not flow out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reads another פסוק in תהלים as דוד describing how worn down he was while his enemies mocked his fall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ובצלעי' (when I limped) point to his stumble with בת שבע. רבא reads 'ולא דמו' as 'and not my blood' (דמי). דוד is saying he was so drained that no blood would come out even if they tore him.

phrases.english: Rava taught: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"And when I limped they rejoiced and gathered,
phrases.notes: תהלים 35:15

phrases.english: the wretched gather themselves together against me,
[and those whom I know not];
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, and they finish off the פסוק.

phrases.english: they tore and did not cease [dammu]"?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: David said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
it is revealed and known before You
that if they were to tear my flesh,
my blood [dami] would not flow.
phrases.notes: רבא is playing on the word דמו from the פסוק and reading it as דמי, 'my blood.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new reading by רבא, still about דוד after the בת שבע episode
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד was so worn out by suffering that tearing his flesh would draw no blood, yet his enemies kept mocking.

steps.title: Shaming someone in public is worse than דוד's sin
steps.stepSummary: דוד continues: scholars stop learning to mock him about adultery, and he answers that public shaming takes away עולם הבא, which his sin does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but when they are learning about the four death penalties of בית דין, they stop their learning and say to me: 'דוד, one who sleeps with a married woman, how is he killed?' I said to them: 'One who sleeps with a married woman is killed by חנק, and he still has a share in עולם הבא. But one who shames his friend in public has no share in עולם הבא.'
steps.whatsHappening: דוד goes on describing his mockers. They bring up his sin in public, and he answers that what they are doing is worse than what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their question is not a real question. It is a way to embarrass דוד in front of everyone. His answer flips it around: even adultery leaves a person with a share in עולם הבא, but public shaming does not. So they are the ones in the bigger trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but; adds something stronger
The four death penalties of the court
Strangulation, one of the four death penalties
One who shames his friend; literally 'makes his face white'
A share in the World to Come

steps.whatToRemember: Shaming another person in public is treated as worse than adultery: it costs a person his share in עולם הבא.
steps.confusionAlert: דוד is not saying adultery is light. It still carries the death penalty of חנק. His point is only that public shaming is even more severe.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for how serious הלבנת פנים (public shaming) is.

phrases.english: And not only that, but
at the time when they are engaged
in the four court-imposed death penalties,
they interrupt their study
and say to me:
David, one who engages in intercourse with a married woman,
his death is with what?
phrases.notes: They are not really asking. They are pointing at his own sin to embarrass him.

phrases.english: I said to them:

phrases.aramaic: הַבָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ מִיתָתוֹ בְּחֶנֶק,
phrases.english: One who engages in intercourse with a married woman, his death is by strangulation,
and he has a share in the World-to-Come.
But one who humiliates another before the multitudes
has no share in the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהֵם עוֹסְקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues דוד's words from step 17, adding a stronger description of the mockery
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adultery is punished by חנק but the sinner keeps עולם הבא. One who shames another in public loses his share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Even while sick, דוד kept his marital duties
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says that even during his illness דוד fulfilled eighteen marital duties, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Even when דוד was sick, he kept eighteen marital duties, as it says: 'I am tired from my groaning; every night I speak in my bed; with my tears I melt my couch.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher, רב יהודה quoting רב, brings another teaching about דוד, this time about his strength even while ill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes him as weak and groaning. Yet it still says 'every night I speak in my bed.' רב reads that as a polite way of describing marital relations. So even in his weakness he did not neglect his wives.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband's marital duty to his wife

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
Even during the time of David's illness
he fulfilled eighteen conjugal duties,
phrases.notes: An עונה is a husband's marital duty. Eighteen means one for each of his wives.

phrases.english: as it is stated:
"I am weary with my groaning;
phrases.notes: תהלים 6:7

phrases.english: every night I speak in my bed;
phrases.notes: 'Speak in my bed' is a polite way of referring to marital relations.

phrases.english: I melt away my couch with tears."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁעַת חׇלְיוֹ שֶׁל דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבא's teachings to a new set of teachings about דוד from רב יהודה in the name of רב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even during his illness, דוד fulfilled his marital duties to all eighteen wives.

steps.title: דוד once wanted to worship idols
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says that דוד wanted to serve עבודה זרה, based on 'when דוד came to the ראש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: דוד wanted to worship idols, as it says: 'And it happened, when דוד came to the ראש, where he would bow down there to God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה brings a second, surprising teaching about דוד: at one low point he wanted to serve idols. The next step will prove why the word ראש points to an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is from the time when דוד was running away from אבשלום. רב reads 'הראש' not as 'the top of the hill' but as a name for an idol. This step only makes the claim. The proof for that reading comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
David sought to engage in idol worship,
as it is stated:
"And it came to pass when David was at the top [rosh]
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 15:32

phrases.english: where he would bow there to God,"

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בִּקֵּשׁ דָּוִד לַעֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same source, רב יהודה in the name of רב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד, at a moment of crisis, wanted to worship idols.

steps.title: Proof that ראש means an idol
steps.stepSummary: The word ראש means an idol, as shown from the image in דניאל whose 'head' (רישיה) was of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ראש means only idol worship, as it says: 'That image, its head was of fine gold.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the reading from the last step: the word ראש is tied to an idol, as we see in ספר דניאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דניאל, the idol-statue is described with the word רישיה, 'its head.' Because the word for 'head' is used for an idol there, רב reads ראש in the פסוק about דוד as an idol too. This is a word-link proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Head, top; here read as an idol

steps.whatToRemember: רב reads ראש in the פסוק about דוד as an idol, because the idol in דניאל is described with the same word, 'head.'

phrases.english: And "rosh" means nothing other than idol worship,
as it is stated:
"As for that image, its head [reishei]
phrases.notes: דניאל 2:32

phrases.english: was of fine gold."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the reading of 'הראש' used in step 20
steps.raayaObject: The reading of 'הראש' in שמואל ב as an idol
steps.raayaSupportSource: דניאל 2:32, where the idol's 'head' (רישיה) is mentioned

steps.title: חושי challenges דוד for wanting to serve idols
steps.stepSummary: Based on the פסוק where חושי comes to meet דוד at the ראש, חושי asks how people could say that a king like דוד served עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says חושי came to meet דוד with a torn coat and earth on his head. חושי said to דוד: Should people say that a king like you served idols?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next פסוק in the story. In it, חושי meets דוד right at the ראש and protests against his plan to serve עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said דוד wanted to serve עבודה זרה at the ראש. Now חושי challenges that plan. A great king serving idols would be a terrible public disgrace.

keyTerms.meaning: his coat torn, a sign of mourning

phrases.english: "And behold, coming to meet him was Hushai the Archite,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 15:32

phrases.english: with his coat torn and earth upon his head."
He said to David:
Shall people say that a king like you
would serve idols?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of דוד at the ראש, which step 21 explained means an idol.
steps.kashyaTarget: דוד's plan to serve עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A famous righteous king serving idols would be a huge public disgrace.

steps.title: דוד explains that idol worship is better than public חילול השם
steps.stepSummary: דוד answers that a righteous king being killed by his own son would be a public חילול השם. Serving idols would be less bad than that.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said to him: Should people say that a king like me was killed by his own son? Better that he serve idols, so that Heaven's name will not be desecrated in public.
steps.whatsHappening: דוד defends his plan. He says the bigger disgrace would be people seeing a righteous king murdered by his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד compares two bad outcomes. If people saw a king who was known to be righteous get killed by his son, they would question Heaven's justice. That is a public חילול השם. If he served idols, his death would look deserved.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of Heaven will be desecrated

phrases.english: He said to him:
A king like me, should his son kill him?
It is better that he serve idols
phrases.notes: דוד is talking about himself as 'he' here.

phrases.english: and that the name of Heaven not be desecrated in public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers חושי's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Serving idols is the worst possible disgrace for a king.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being killed by his son with no visible cause would be a worse public חילול השם.

steps.title: חושי asks why דוד married a יפת תואר
steps.stepSummary: חושי asks דוד why he married a יפת תואר. This question sets up חושי's answer to דוד's worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: חושי said: Why did you marry a beautiful captive woman?
steps.whatsHappening: חושי asks דוד a question about his marriage. It is setting up the next move, where חושי will explain why there would be no חילול השם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question seems to change the subject, but it is aimed straight at דוד's argument. אבשלום's mother was a יפת תואר. חושי is about to tie that fact to אבשלום's rebellion.

keyTerms.meaning: a beautiful captive woman taken in war, whom the תורה allows a soldier to marry

phrases.english: He said: What is the reason
that you married a beautiful captive woman?
phrases.notes: He means אבשלום's mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: חושי begins his reply to דוד's argument about חילול השם.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why דוד chose to marry a יפת תואר.

steps.title: דוד answers that the תורה permits a יפת תואר
steps.stepSummary: דוד answers that the תורה itself allows marrying a יפת תואר.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said to him: The Merciful One, the תורה, permitted a beautiful captive woman.
steps.whatsHappening: דוד defends his marriage. He says it was fully allowed by the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד's point is that he did nothing wrong. The marriage was permitted, so it cannot be held against him.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning הקדוש ברוך הוא in His תורה

phrases.english: He said to him:
A beautiful captive woman, the Merciful One permitted her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers חושי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה explicitly permits marrying a יפת תואר.

steps.title: The סמוכין: a יפת תואר leads to a בן סורר ומורה
steps.stepSummary: חושי points to the סמוכין. The פרשה of בן סורר ומורה comes right after the פרשה of יפת תואר, which teaches that marrying a יפת תואר leads to a rebellious son. So people will blame אבשלום's mother, not Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: חושי said to him: Didn't you learn from the verses placed next to each other? Right next to it is written, 'If a man has a wayward and rebellious son.' Anyone who marries a beautiful captive woman will have a wayward and rebellious son.
steps.whatsHappening: חושי pushes back on דוד's whole argument. He uses the order of the פסוקים to show that people will understand why אבשלום rebelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permitted is not the same as wise. The תורה places בן סורר ומורה next to יפת תואר to warn what such a marriage leads to. So if אבשלום kills דוד, people will blame the mother, there is no חילול השם, and דוד has no reason to serve idols.

keyTerms.meaning: learning from two פרשיות that are placed next to each other
which is placed right next to it

steps.whatToRemember: חושי turns דוד's argument around: because of the יפת תואר, אבשלום's rebellion has an explanation, so there is no חילול השם and no excuse to serve idols.
steps.confusionAlert: חושי is not saying the marriage was forbidden. It was permitted. He is saying that the סמוכין shows its result is predictable, so people will not blame Heaven.

phrases.english: He said to him: Did you not learn from juxtaposed verses,
since right next to it is written:
"If a man has a wayward and rebellious son"?
phrases.notes: דברים 21:18

phrases.english: Anyone who marries a beautiful captive woman
will have a wayward and rebellious son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to דוד's defense from step 25, and through it his whole argument in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: דוד's claim that his death at אבשלום's hands would cause a public חילול השם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סמוכין give a clear reason for אבשלום's rebellion, so people will not blame Heaven.

steps.title: רבי דוסתאי compares דוד to a bargaining merchant
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי from בירי teaches that דוד is like a כותי merchant. This sets up the next step, where דוד asks for forgiveness bit by bit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסתאי from בירי taught: What is דוד like? He is like a כותי merchant.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins with a comparison. It is setting up the next move, where we see דוד bargaining with הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A merchant bargains one small step at a time. The comparison prepares us to see דוד make bigger and bigger requests, each one built on the last.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dostai from Beirei expounded:
To what is David comparable?
To a Cuthean merchant.
phrases.notes: Such a merchant bargains bit by bit. Watch how דוד asks for a little more each time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about דוד's sin and forgiveness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד is like a merchant who bargains step by step.

steps.title: דוד asks forgiveness step by step and is forgiven
steps.stepSummary: Using the פסוקים in תהלים 19, דוד asks to be forgiven for errors, then hidden sins, then intentional sins, and then that the רבנן not speak about him. Each time הקדוש ברוך הוא answers 'שביקי לך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world, 'Who can understand errors!' He said to him: They are forgiven for you. 'Cleanse me from hidden sins!' They are forgiven for you. 'Also from intentional sins hold back Your servant!' They are forgiven for you. 'Let them not rule over me, then I will be whole,' meaning the רבנן should not talk about me. They are forgiven for you.
steps.whatsHappening: This shows the merchant comparison in action. דוד keeps raising his request, and each one is granted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The requests grow step by step. They go from accidental sins, to private sins, to deliberate sins, to his public reputation among the רבנן. This is exactly how a merchant keeps pushing for a little more.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: David said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world, "Who can understand errors!"
phrases.notes: תהלים 19:13

phrases.english: [He said to him:] They are forgiven for you.
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets. They make clear that God is the one answering.

phrases.english: "And cleanse me from hidden sins!"
They are forgiven for you.
"Also from intentional sins hold back Your servant!"
phrases.notes: תהלים 19:14

phrases.english: They are forgiven for you.
"Let them not rule over me, then I will be whole,"
meaning that the Rabbis should not talk about me.
They are forgiven for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the merchant comparison from step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד bargained with הקדוש ברוך הוא like a merchant.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 19:13-14, read as a series of growing requests.

steps.title: דוד asks that his sin not be written, and is refused
steps.stepSummary: דוד next asks that his great sin not be written in the תנ"ך. הקדוש ברוך הוא says this is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And I will be clean from great transgression,' meaning that my sin should not be written. He said to him: It is impossible.
steps.whatsHappening: דוד makes a bigger request: to erase the record of his sin. For the first time, the answer is no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every earlier request was granted. This one is refused. Forgiveness is possible, but removing the story from the written תורה is not.
steps.confusionAlert: Being refused here does not take back the forgiveness. Only the request to erase the written record is denied.

phrases.english: "And I will be clean from great transgression,"
that my sin should not be written.
phrases.notes: He means his sin with בת שבע and אוריה.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is impossible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next, larger request in the series, and the first one refused.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's sin cannot be left out of the written record.

steps.title: קל וחומר from the יוד taken from שרי
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא proves His refusal with a קל וחומר. A single יוד removed from שרי's name cried out for years until it was given to יהושע. An entire פרשה certainly cannot be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a יוד that I took from שרי stood and cried out for many years, until יהושע came and I added it to his name, as it says, 'And משה called הושע son of נון, יהושע', then an entire section, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: This gives the reason why דוד's sin must stay written. It uses a קל וחומר from a single letter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name שרי became שרה, which removed a יוד. That one letter protested until it was added to הושע to make יהושע. If one letter cannot just disappear from the תורה, a whole פרשה surely cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: all the more so, the wording of a קל וחומר

steps.whatToRemember: דוד was forgiven at every level, but his sin stays written in the תנ"ך. Not even one letter of the תורה is lost, so an entire פרשה certainly cannot be.

phrases.english: And if a yud that I took from Sarai
phrases.notes: When her name was changed from שרי to שרה, the יוד was dropped.

phrases.english: stood and cried out for many years,
until Joshua came and I added it to him,
as it is stated:
"And Moses called Hoshea son of Nun, Yehoshua."
phrases.notes: במדבר 13:16

phrases.english: then an entire section,
how much more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the refusal in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד's sin cannot be left out of the written record.
steps.raayaSupportSource: קל וחומר from the יוד of שרי, given to יהושע (במדבר 13:16).

steps.title: דוד asks to be forgiven for the entire sin
steps.stepSummary: Using the next words of תהלים 19, 'ונקיתי מפשע רב', דוד asks הקדוש ברוך הוא to forgive the whole sin completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And I shall be clear from great transgression." He said before Him: Master of the Universe, forgive me for that entire sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues reading the פסוקים of תהלים 19 as דוד's requests. Now דוד asks for the biggest thing: complete forgiveness for the whole sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, דוד asked for forgiveness step by step and was answered 'שביקי לך' each time. Here the request grows to 'כולו', the entire sin, with nothing left over. This sets up הקדוש ברוך הוא's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will be cleared / found clean

phrases.english: "And I shall be clear from great transgression."
phrases.notes: תהלים 19:14

phrases.english: He said before Him:
Master of the Universe,

phrases.aramaic: מְחוֹל לִי עַל אוֹתוֹ עָוֹן כּוּלּוֹ!
phrases.english: forgive me for that entire sin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list of requests from תהלים 19 (step 28) after the side point about the פרשה staying in the תנ"ך, and gives the last and biggest request.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד asks for complete forgiveness of the whole sin, read into 'ונקיתי מפשע רב'.

steps.title: God refuses, quoting שלמה's verse about fire and coals
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers that שלמה will one day write that a man cannot carry fire without being burned. In the same way, a man who sins with another man's wife cannot be fully cleared.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Your son שלמה is already going to say in his wisdom: "Can a man take fire into his lap and his clothes not be burned? Can a man walk on hot coals and his feet not be scorched? So too, one who goes to his neighbor's wife; whoever touches her will not be cleared."
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא turns down דוד's request for total forgiveness. He backs up the refusal with a פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד asked to be 'ונקיתי', cleared. The פסוק answers with the same root: 'לא ינקה', he will not be cleared. Just as fire must burn, this sin must leave some mark, so it cannot be wiped away for free.

keyTerms.meaning: Will not be cleared / go unpunished

phrases.english: He said,
your son Solomon is already destined
to say in his wisdom:
"Can a man take fire into his lap
and his clothes not be burned?
Can a man walk on hot coals
and his feet not be scorched?
So too, one who goes to his neighbor's wife;
whoever touches her will not be cleared."
phrases.notes: Notice the match: דוד asked 'ונקיתי', to be cleared, and this פסוק says 'לא ינקה', he won't be.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר כְּבָר עָתִיד שְׁלֹמֹה בִּנְךָ לוֹמַר בְּחׇכְמָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns down the request of step 31 and supports the refusal with a פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the request for total, cost-free forgiveness of the whole sin.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A sin with another man's wife always leaves a mark, like fire that must burn. So it cannot be completely cleared.

steps.title: דוד asks whether he is lost forever
steps.stepSummary: דוד pushes back: is 'that man', meaning himself, so completely rejected that there is no way back?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to Him: Is that man rejected to such an extent?
steps.whatsHappening: דוד challenges the refusal and asks whether it means he is cast away with no fix at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The refusal sounded final, so דוד asks if there is truly no remedy. He speaks of himself as 'that man' instead of saying 'I'. This sets up the solution in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: So much / to such an extent
That man (a polite way of saying 'I')

phrases.english: He said to Him:
Is that man rejected to such an extent?
phrases.notes: 'That man' is דוד talking about himself; the גמרא uses this phrase to avoid saying something bad directly about the speaker.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ כֹּל הָכִי נִטְרַד הָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the refusal in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The refusal in step 32 that דוד cannot be fully cleared.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no forgiveness is possible, דוד would be rejected forever. Can that really be the result?

steps.title: The solution: accept suffering, and דוד accepts
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא tells דוד to take יסורין upon himself, and דוד agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Accept afflictions upon yourself. He accepted them.
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא gives דוד a way back: accept suffering. דוד accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin cannot be erased for free, but דוד is not lost forever. The 'mark' the sin must leave comes as יסורין, and the יסורין open the path to atonement. This sets up רב's description of those יסורין in the next step.
steps.whatToRemember: דוד could not get his sin wiped away for free ('לא ינקה'), but he was not rejected. He accepted יסורין as his path to atonement.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Accept afflictions upon yourself.
He accepted them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers דוד's pushback in step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a middle path: no free forgiveness, but atonement through suffering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the sin cannot be cleared, דוד would be rejected forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: Accepting יסורין lets דוד atone without the sin being wiped away for free.

steps.title: רב: six months of צרעת, losing the שכינה, and the סנהדרין's distance
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says that for six months דוד had צרעת, the שכינה left him, and the סנהדרין stayed away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רב said: For six months דוד was struck with צרעת, the שכינה departed from him, and the סנהדרין separated from him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement from רב describes what דוד's יסורין actually were. It lists three things, and the next steps will prove each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fills in step 34, which only said דוד accepted יסורין. רב names three kinds of suffering: in his body (צרעת), in his spiritual life (the שכינה), and with other people (the סנהדרין). He also says it lasted six months, and the גמרא will ask where that number comes from.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
For six months David was struck with tzaraas,
and the Shechina departed from him,
and the Sanhedrin separated from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים נִצְטָרַע דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what the יסורין accepted in step 34 actually were.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's יסורין were six months of צרעת, losing the שכינה, and being avoided by the סנהדרין.

steps.title: Proof that דוד had צרעת
steps.stepSummary: The צרעת is proven from 'תחטאני באזוב', because hyssop is used to purify a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was struck with צרעת, as it is written: "Purge me with hyssop and I will be pure; wash me and I will be whiter than snow."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first part of רב's statement, that דוד had צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פרק of תהלים, דוד asks to be purified with אזוב and to become white as snow. Purifying with אזוב is part of the process for a מצורע, so the פסוק shows he needed that kind of purification.

keyTerms.meaning: Hyssop, a plant used in purification

phrases.english: He was struck with tzaraas, as it is written:
"Purge me with hyssop and I will be pure;
phrases.notes: תהלים 51:9. אזוב is used when a מצורע becomes pure, which is why this hints at צרעת.

phrases.english: wash me and I will be whiter than snow."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first of רב's three claims.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד was struck with צרעת.

steps.title: Proof that the שכינה left דוד
steps.stepSummary: 'השיבה לי ששון ישעך', 'bring back to me', shows that something holy had been taken away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שכינה departed from him, as it is written: "Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and let a generous spirit support me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second part of רב's statement, that the שכינה left דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only ask for something to be 'brought back' if it is gone. דוד asking for the joy and the spirit to return shows that the שכינה had left him.

phrases.english: The Shechina departed from him, as it is written:
"Restore to me the joy of Your salvation,
phrases.notes: תהלים 51:14. 'Restore' means it had been taken away.

phrases.english: and let a generous spirit support me."

steps.triggerLanguage: נִסְתַּלְּקָה הֵימֶנּוּ שְׁכִינָה דִּכְתִיב הָשִׁיבָה לִּי שְׂשׂוֹן יִשְׁעֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second of רב's three claims.

steps.title: Proof that the סנהדרין stayed away from דוד
steps.stepSummary: 'ישובו לי יראיך', 'let those who fear You return to me', shows that the חכמים had pulled away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The סנהדרין separated from him, as it is written: "Let those who fear You return to me," and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the third part of רב's statement, that the סנהדרין stayed away from דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Those who fear You' are understood as the God-fearing חכמים of the סנהדרין. Asking them to 'return' shows they had left him.

phrases.english: And the Sanhedrin separated from him, as it is written:
"Let those who fear You return to me," and so on.
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:79. Again, 'return' tells us they had gone away.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפֵרְשׁוּ מִמֶּנּוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין דִּכְתִיב יָשׁוּבוּ לִי יְרֵאֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the third of רב's three claims.
steps.raayaObject: That the סנהדרין separated from דוד.

steps.title: Where do we know it was six months?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רב's number, six months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Six months, from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: Three of רב's claims have now been proven, but not the length of time. The גמרא asks where the 'six months' comes from, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים in תהלים show what happened, but they do not say how long it lasted. So the number needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Six months, from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the one part of רב's statement (step 35) that has not been proven yet.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that דוד's יסורין lasted six months.

steps.title: The answer begins: דוד reigned forty years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer with the פסוק that says דוד ruled over ישראל for forty years. The rest of the proof continues afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And the days that דוד reigned over ישראל were forty years."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question about six months by quoting a פסוק about how long דוד was king. The full proof continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plan is to work out the six months from the count of דוד's years as king. Here the גמרא only lays down the starting point, forty years. The details that produce six months come next.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the days that David reigned
over Israel were forty years."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 2:11. The proof isn't finished yet; it keeps going right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב וְהַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר מָלַךְ דָּוִד עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The six months will be worked out from the פסוק giving the length of דוד's reign, starting with 'forty years'. The rest of the proof follows.
